recognize_zh: 低倍骨髓切片中，箭頭標示一片邊界不清、呈淡粉紅色的組織球聚集區，與周圍深染的造血細胞形成對比，是鬆散、未成熟的肉芽腫（poorly formed granuloma）。
features: Ill-defined pale eosinophilic nodular area (arrows) within cellular marrow
Loose aggregate of histiocytes with pale cytoplasm rather than a compact epithelioid granuloma
No well-formed multinucleated giant cells or caseous necrosis evident at this power
Surrounding hypercellular marrow with mixed hematopoietic cells
Organisms not resolvable at this low magnification
describe_en: Low-power view of the bone marrow biopsy shows a hypercellular marrow containing an ill-defined, pale eosinophilic aggregate of histiocytes (arrows) that blends with the surrounding hematopoietic elements. The lesion lacks a sharp border, well-formed giant cells or caseous necrosis. Intracellular organisms cannot be assessed at this magnification. Findings are consistent with a poorly formed (loose) granuloma; in the clinical setting, GMS and PAS stains are recommended and are compatible with disseminated histoplasmosis.

ddx.vs: Tuberculous granulomas are more often compact with epithelioid cells, Langhans giant cells and caseous necrosis, and are identified with AFB stain.
Lipogranulomas are small aggregates of histiocytes around clear lipid vacuoles and are usually incidental.
Hodgkin lymphoma shows a fibrotic polymorphous infiltrate with Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells that are CD30 and CD15 positive.
Mast cell aggregates are composed of spindled cells with pale cytoplasm and eosinophils and are tryptase/CD117/CD25 positive.
